value_chain.value_chain_position: Core model creation layer with a research-first, cost-efficiency focus. DeepSeek is fully funded by High-Flyer, a Chinese quantitative hedge fund ($8B AUM) co-founded by CEO Liang Wenfeng. It depends on NVIDIA GPUs (H100, H800, H20) for training compute, with approximately 50,000 Hopper-generation GPUs, and is actively diversifying toward Huawei Ascend AI chips for inference and smaller models. Downstream, DeepSeek serves the global developer ecosystem through its API platform and consumer chatbot app. Its open-weight models (MIT license) are widely hosted by third-party inference providers (Together AI, Fireworks AI, Deep Infra, NVIDIA NIM, major cloud providers), making it a foundational dependency for a rapidly growing open-source AI ecosystem.

key_products: DeepSeek-V3.2 (Dec 2025): frontier general-purpose LLM using Mixture-of-Experts (671B total parameters, ~37B active), 128K context window. Achieves GPT-5-level performance on major benchmarks at a fraction of the cost. V3.2-Speciale variant surpasses GPT-5-High on AIME (96.0% vs 94.6%) and achieves gold-medal performance on IOI, ICPC, IMO, and CMO 2025. Pricing: $0.26/$0.39 per M tokens (input/output).

DeepSeek-R1 (Jan 2025): reasoning model trained with pure reinforcement learning (GRPO), matching OpenAI o1 performance at 90-95% lower cost. 128K context, up to 64K output tokens. Trained for $5.6M using 2,048 GPUs. Released under MIT license. R1 0528 update (May 2025) with further improvements. Pricing: $0.55/$2.19 per M tokens.

DeepSeek consumer app and API platform: free chatbot app (75M+ downloads, 97M MAU as of Apr 2025), ranked #1 in App Store across 156 countries. API is OpenAI-compatible (drop-in replacement), with 5M free tokens for new accounts. Handles 5.7B API calls/month.

business.revenue_or_valuation: Annualized revenue run rate ~$220M as of mid-2025, primarily from API and enterprise services. No external valuation -- DeepSeek has raised $0 in traditional VC funding. The company is 84% owned by founder Liang Wenfeng, with the remainder held by individuals affiliated with High-Flyer. Reportedly considering first outside funding round (early 2025 reports) but no round has closed as of Feb 2026.
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: $220M annualized run rate as of mid-2025, driven by API usage (5.7B calls/month) and 26,000+ enterprise accounts. Revenue reportedly covers ongoing operational costs. [uncertain]
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Zero external VC funding. Entirely self-funded by Liang Wenfeng through profits from High-Flyer hedge fund ($8B AUM). Total capital investment estimated at $1.6B in servers plus ~$944M in operating costs. Liang personally bankrolls the operation, having been turned off by VCs' focus on rapid monetization over fundamental research.
business.business_model: Usage-based API pricing (primary revenue driver) plus free consumer app with optional premium features. API pricing is the lowest among frontier model providers: DeepSeek-V3.2 at $0.26/$0.39 per M tokens, R1 at $0.55/$2.19, with cache hits as low as $0.028/M tokens. Off-peak pricing offers 50-75% discounts. OpenAI-compatible API format enables frictionless adoption. Enterprise accounts (26,000+) and third-party inference providers also distribute the models.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: Estimated $1.6B total investment in GPU infrastructure, ~$944M in operating costs. Revenue reportedly covers ongoing costs as of mid-2025. With only ~160 employees and High-Flyer's $8B AUM backing, burn rate is substantially lower than Western competitors. [uncertain]

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Fully open-source (MIT license). DeepSeek-R1, V3, V3.1, and V3.2 model weights are all released under the permissive MIT license, allowing unrestricted commercial use, derivative development, and proprietary products without profit-sharing. Earlier models used a custom OpenRAIL-based license, but DeepSeek unified to MIT in 2025. Distilled variants (e.g., R1-Distill-Qwen-32B) are released under Apache 2.0. Training code and full training data are not disclosed, but architecture details are published in technical papers. This is the most permissive licensing among any frontier-class model provider.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: DeepSeek is arguably the most disruptive force in the AI model landscape for entrepreneurs. Key considerations: (1) Cost revolution: DeepSeek's API pricing ($0.26/M input tokens for V3.2) is 10-50x cheaper than equivalent Western frontier models, fundamentally changing unit economics for AI-powered startups -- what was unaffordable becomes viable; (2) MIT license freedom: unlike Meta's Llama (community license with restrictions) or OpenAI (closed), DeepSeek's MIT license allows startups to self-host, fine-tune, and build proprietary products with zero licensing overhead or usage reporting -- maximum commercial freedom; (3) OpenAI-compatible API: drop-in replacement for OpenAI's API format means startups can switch providers with minimal code changes, reducing vendor lock-in risk; (4) Efficiency breakthrough narrative: DeepSeek proved that frontier-class AI can be built for $5.6M (R1 training cost) instead of hundreds of millions, validating the thesis that algorithmic innovation can overcome compute disadvantage -- encouraging for resource-constrained startups; (5) Third-party hosting ecosystem: DeepSeek models are available on Together AI, Fireworks, Deep Infra, AWS, Azure, GCP, and more, giving startups deployment flexibility; (6) Geopolitical risk: as a Chinese company storing data in China, DeepSeek faces bans and restrictions in some markets (Italy API suspension, Germany app blocking), and potential US export control implications -- startups in regulated sectors should consider self-hosting the open-weight models instead of using DeepSeek's API directly; (7) The 160-person team model demonstrates that lean, research-focused organizations can compete with billion-dollar labs -- an inspiration for technical founders.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Extremely high accessibility -- the most accessible frontier AI available. Free consumer app (iOS/Android/web). Free API tier with 5M tokens for new accounts. Pay-as-you-go API from $0.028/M tokens (cache hit) to $2.19/M tokens (R1 output). Off-peak discounts of 50-75%. No subscription required. OpenAI-compatible API format. Open-weight models (MIT license) available for self-hosting via Hugging Face, NVIDIA NIM, and all major cloud providers. No startup program needed -- the base pricing is already lower than most providers' startup credits.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: None. DeepSeek is a foundation model creator.

ecosystem.key_partnerships: Huawei: strategic chip partnership for Ascend AI GPUs, with DeepSeek adopting Huawei chips for smaller model inference to reduce NVIDIA dependency. NVIDIA: primary GPU supplier (H100, H800, H20) for training infrastructure. Third-party inference providers: Together AI, Fireworks AI, Deep Infra, SiliconFlow host DeepSeek models. Major cloud providers: AWS, Azure, GCP all offer DeepSeek models. 20+ global tech giants announced DeepSeek integration (Feb 2025). No formal VC or strategic investor relationships due to self-funding model.
ecosystem.competitive_moat: Algorithmic efficiency leadership: DeepSeek's innovations (MoE architecture, GRPO reinforcement learning, sparse attention, synthetic data rejection sampling) deliver frontier performance at a fraction of competitors' training and inference costs. Open-source ecosystem lock-in: MIT license has driven massive community adoption (75M+ app downloads, 5.7B monthly API calls, thousands of derivative models on Hugging Face), creating a network effect where developers build tooling and applications around DeepSeek models. Cost structure advantage: 160-person team with High-Flyer backing operates at dramatically lower overhead than Western labs (OpenAI ~2,000 employees, Anthropic ~1,000), enabling aggressive pricing that competitors struggle to match. Research publication transparency: detailed technical papers attract top talent and build developer trust.

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: Complex and adversarial regulatory position. EU AI Act: DeepSeek R1 is below the 10^25 FLOPs threshold for automatic systemic risk classification, but EU regulators may designate it as systemic risk due to its widespread adoption. DeepSeek has NOT signed the EU GPAI Code of Practice. GDPR: Italy's Garante suspended DeepSeek API access (Sep 2025) for GDPR violations on international data transfers. Germany moved to block the app from app stores (Jun 2025). DeepSeek has claimed GDPR does not apply to it as a China-based company, a position EU regulators reject. Data sovereignty: all user data processed through DeepSeek's API is stored in China, raising concerns for enterprises in regulated sectors. US export controls: DeepSeek operates under US chip export restrictions, having stockpiled NVIDIA GPUs before bans took effect and now diversifying to Huawei chips. Multiple countries have investigated or restricted DeepSeek access.
